premise: At 57 I raided my $60,000 factory pension to fund my brother’s backyard vertical‑farming startup, shaking hands on a 30% share and a seat on the board; once he landed a $900,000 supermarket contract, he sent me a check for $62,000 and a letter dissolving our arrangement. I proved the verbal contract through years of text messages, sued for promissory estoppel, and was awarded $280,000 in lost equity — I used the settlement to buy a competing hydroponic warehouse, now supply the same supermarket chain with ‘Legacy Greens,’ and a QR code on every package links to the court opinion and his deposition perjury.
